rows.grounds: anaphoric pronoun referring to the self under discussion
compound of prāṇa and rūpī, formed of breath or life-force
locative indicating the seat of the supreme self
compound of parama and ātmaka, having supreme-self nature

items.question: What is the relation between the prāṇa-formed self and the supreme self in the heart?
premises: The supreme self resides in heart.
items.inference: Thus the embodied self is breath-formed while the supreme self abides in the heart.
uncertainties: The exact referent of sa is not explicit in this verse.
items.plain_english: He is the self formed of prāṇa, but the supreme self is in the heart.
